description: Engineering software that works, scales and can be maintained: processes, requirements, modelling, architecture and design, user interfaces, verification, testing, maintenance and the management of teams, all exercised in a term-long team project. Taught to the depth of a leading software engineering course.
modelledOn: Pressman and Maxim, Software Engineering: A Practitioner's Approach
Fox and Patterson, Engineering Software as a Service: An Agile Approach Using Cloud Computing
IEEE SWEBOK Guide to the Software Engineering Body of Knowledge
outcomes: Compare software process models and choose and tailor one for a given project.
Elicit, specify, validate and manage requirements with user stories and formal specifications.
Model systems with UML and design them with sound architecture and design principles and patterns.
Design user interfaces that follow established principles and are evaluated with users.
Verify and validate software with reviews, static analysis and tests at unit, integration and system level.
Plan maintenance and evolution and manage a software team with agile practices and measurable progress.

units.title: Software engineering and process models
topics: What software engineering is; the cost of failure (Therac-25, Ariane 5, local e-government projects)
Software processes: waterfall, incremental, spiral, RUP; agile methods: XP, Scrum, Kanban; DevOps
Process activities: specification, development, validation, evolution
Choosing and tailoring a process; process improvement and CMMI in brief
Project team formation and tooling: Git, issue tracker, CI

units.title: Software requirements
topics: Functional and non-functional requirements; quality attributes
Elicitation: interviews, observation, workshops, prototypes, scenarios; stakeholders
User stories, acceptance criteria, use cases; the software requirements specification
Requirements validation, prioritisation (MoSCoW), traceability and change management
Formal specification in brief: pre- and post-conditions, invariants

units.title: System models with UML
topics: Context, interaction, structural and behavioural models
Use case, activity, sequence, class, state machine, component and deployment diagrams
Model-driven engineering in brief; keeping models and code consistent
Modelling the team project

units.title: Architectural design
topics: Architecture and its influence on quality attributes; architectural views
Patterns: layered, client-server, MVC, pipe-and-filter, repository, microservices, event-driven
Application architectures: transaction processing, information systems, language processing
Documenting architecture; architectural decision records

units.title: Design and implementation
topics: Object-oriented design process; design principles: SOLID, cohesion and coupling, information hiding
Design patterns: Observer, Strategy, Factory, Adapter, Facade, Command, Singleton and when not to use them
Implementation issues: reuse, configuration management, host-target development, open source and licensing
Code quality: style, reviews, refactoring, technical debt, static analysis
APIs, interfaces and contracts; defensive programming and error handling

units.title: User interface design principles
topics: User-centred design; usability principles and heuristics; consistency, feedback, error recovery
Interaction styles; information presentation; colour and accessibility
Prototyping and evaluating the team project's interface with users
Internationalisation and designing for low-end devices

units.title: Verification and validation
topics: Verification versus validation; the V-model; inspections and reviews
Static analysis, linters, type checkers, model checking in brief
Test planning; test-driven development; code coverage and its limits
Formal methods and when they are worth it; safety-critical systems

units.title: Software testing
topics: Unit testing with a framework; mocks and stubs; property-based testing
Black-box techniques: equivalence partitioning, boundary values, decision tables; white-box: statement, branch, path coverage
Integration, system, acceptance, regression, performance, security and usability testing
Test automation in CI; test documentation and defect tracking

units.title: Software maintenance and evolution
topics: Lehman's laws; types of maintenance; the cost of change
Legacy systems: assessment, reengineering, migration, strangler pattern
Refactoring, continuous evolution, release management and versioning
Software metrics for maintainability and quality

units.title: Project and team management
topics: Risk management, estimation (story points, COCOMO in brief), scheduling, tracking velocity and burndown
Teamwork: roles, communication, motivation, conflict; distributed and remote teams
Quality management and standards (ISO 9001, ISO/IEC 25010); configuration management
Professional ethics and the ACM/IEEE code; project presentation and retrospective

schedule.title: Software engineering and development processes
schedule.exercise: Short essay: use a real software failure (for example a national ID or e-government system) to argue which process model would have reduced the risk, with three specific reasons.

tasks.title: Match six project descriptions in a scenario to the process model (waterfall, incremental, Scrum or Kanban) that fits best and justify each
Analyse a failed software project case, find the three decisions that caused the failure, and say what each cost, scored on the rubric
Draw the process activities of an agile team for one sprint as a BPMN diagram, showing specification, development, validation and evolution tasks with hand-offs

schedule.title: Process choice and team tooling
schedule.exercise: Set up a team repository with branches, an issue tracker and a CI check for a small project, and write down the team's working agreement on reviews.

tasks.title: Create a git repository, make three commits on a feature branch, merge it to main, and show the history log
Resolve a merge conflict between two feature branches in git and describe what each side changed and how you chose the final code
Tailor a process for a four-person student team with a fixed deadline in a branching case, choosing practices and defending each against the rubric

schedule.title: Requirements engineering
schedule.exercise: Write ten requirements for a school-fees payment system as five functional and five non-functional, each testable and measurable, plus three user stories with acceptance criteria.

tasks.title: Classify twelve statements in a scenario as functional requirements, non-functional requirements or design decisions
Write five user stories with acceptance criteria and draw a use case diagram for a clinic appointment system
Elicit requirements from three stakeholders with conflicting needs in a branching case, choosing methods and resolving conflicts, scored on the rubric

schedule.title: Requirements validation and formal specification
schedule.exercise: Prioritise twenty requirements with MoSCoW for a fixed budget, build a traceability table to test cases, and write pre- and post-conditions for two functions.

tasks.title: Sort fifteen requirements into Must, Should, Could and Won't in a scenario, given a fixed sprint budget
Build a traceability matrix linking ten requirements to design elements and test cases, and spot the requirement with no test
Write pre- and post-conditions and invariants for a bank account class, then add runtime assertions that catch five faulty calls

schedule.title: System modelling with UML
schedule.exercise: Model a library or clinic system with a use case, class, sequence and state diagram, and check the diagrams stay consistent with each other.

tasks.title: Draw a class diagram of six classes for an online shop with attributes, methods and multiplicities
Draw a sequence diagram for the checkout use case and the matching state machine for an order
Model the team project with context, use case, class, sequence and deployment diagrams, then check each diagram agrees with the others and fix any inconsistency

schedule.title: Software architecture
schedule.exercise: Document the architecture of a mobile money app with two views, one pattern choice, a quality attribute scenario and an architecture decision record.

tasks.title: Draw a layered architecture for a web application and label the responsibilities of each layer
Draw monolith, microservices and event-driven architectures for the same order system and compare their latency, scaling and deployment effort
Choose an architecture for a national health information system in a branching case, trading off availability, cost and offline operation, and record the decisions

schedule.title: Object-oriented design and patterns
schedule.exercise: Refactor a given class that violates SOLID into smaller classes, and apply one design pattern, explaining what coupling it removes.

tasks.title: Identify which SOLID principle is broken in a given class and refactor it with a short test showing the behaviour is the same
Apply the Strategy pattern to remove a long conditional for payment methods and add a new method without changing existing code
Implement Observer and Factory for a notification service, and write tests showing a new channel can be added without changing the core code

schedule.title: Code quality and defensive design
schedule.exercise: Review a 60-line function: list five code smells, refactor it in small steps with tests passing, and note the technical debt left.

tasks.title: Run a linter on a given program, fix every warning, and note which warnings pointed to real defects
Refactor a long function with duplicated code into small functions under a test suite and show that tests pass after each step
Add input checks and error handling to a given API so it rejects ten malformed inputs safely, with a contract stated for each function

schedule.title: User interface design in the process
schedule.exercise: Evaluate a ticketing app's interface for consistency, feedback and error recovery with three users, and adapt it for low-end phones.

tasks.title: Spot ten usability violations (consistency, feedback and error recovery) in a described app and name the principle broken by each
Draw a paper prototype of three screens for a clinic appointment app, then revise it after a described user test
Plan the internationalisation of a Ghanaian bill-payment app for English, Twi and Ewe on low-end devices in a branching case and decide the trade-offs

schedule.title: Verification, validation and static checking
schedule.exercise: Hold a 30-minute code inspection on a short program using a checklist, and record defects found, effort spent and defects per hour.

tasks.title: Place six activities (inspection, unit test, acceptance test and others) on the V-model in a scenario according to the phase they check
Write failing tests first and then the code (TDD) for a discount calculator, and report statement and branch coverage reached
Decide whether formal methods are justified for three systems (an infusion pump, a shop app and a payment switch) in a case and defend each choice

schedule.title: Software testing techniques
schedule.exercise: Design a test suite for a function using equivalence classes, boundary values and a decision table, and report the coverage of statements and branches.

tasks.title: Choose equivalence classes and boundary values for a grading function that maps marks to grades, and write the test cases
Write unit tests with mocks and stubs for a service that calls a payment gateway, and cover a timeout and a refusal
Raise branch coverage on a given function from 55 to 95 percent, then show that a mutation still survives and explain what test is missing

schedule.title: Maintenance, legacy systems and releases
schedule.exercise: Write a short plan to migrate a legacy payroll system with the strangler pattern: first slices, the tests that protect behaviour and the release strategy.

tasks.title: Tag three releases of a small project with semantic version numbers in git and write a changelog that records each change
Classify twelve change requests in a scenario as corrective, adaptive, perfective or preventive maintenance, and estimate the cost of each
Plan the modernisation of a legacy system in a branching case, choosing between rewrite, reengineering and the strangler pattern with risk evidence

schedule.title: Project management, ethics and the final project
schedule.exercise: Final project deliverable: plan, estimate and present a team project, with a risk register, a burndown chart, a quality plan and a retrospective on ethics.

tasks.title: Draw a burndown chart for a two-week sprint from given daily remaining-work data and say whether the team is on track
Estimate a project with story points and COCOMO, build a schedule with dependencies, and identify the critical path and top three risks
Resolve an ethics dilemma in a branching case (a deadline pressing a release with a known safety defect) using the professional code, scored on the rubric
